expectations.text: Proposes no fourth code change to the test or the app (no code block that edits dashboard.spec.ts or a component; a diagnostic command is fine)
expectations.evidence: No fenced code block and no edit to dashboard.spec.ts or the component. The only file-touching instruction is diagnostic: "Add `screenshot: 'only-on-failure'` and `trace: 'retain-on-failure'` to the `use` block in `playwright.config.ts`" (enabling capture), plus checks for a stale CI checkout or build cache, none of which change test or app behavior.

expectations.text: Names one specific assumption behind the previous three fixes that may be wrong (for example: that the heading renders at all on CI, that CI has a backend to talk to, that auth state or viewport on CI matches local)
expectations.evidence: "All three fixes so far assumed the heading renders late, just slowly or awkwardly selected."

expectations.text: Asks for evidence rather than guessing: requests a CI artifact (trace, screenshot, video, console log, or the failing run's HTML report)
expectations.evidence: "Open the log from the most recent failing run" and "Open the result: `npx playwright show-trace <path-to-trace.zip>`, or the screenshot directly."

expectations.text: States plainly, in one sentence, that it is stopping the change-and-retry loop, without apology
expectations.evidence: "Confirm which, instead of guessing again:" plainly rejects further guess-and-check in favor of confirmation, with no apology, before listing the diagnostic steps.

expectations.text: No dramatized tone ('Uh oh', 'Oh no', 'There seems to be a problem'); matter-of-fact

suggestions.reason: At 2079 chars this is nearly double the limit, but the length is spent on a genuinely useful branch (distinguishing 'the fix never reached CI' from 'the fix reached CI and the shared assumption is wrong') rather than padding. Every run in both arms exceeds 1200 chars; the threshold may be testing terseness at the expense of the diagnostic depth the scenario invites.

eval_feedback.overall: Content assertions hold up well; the length assertion conflicts with the depth the scenario invites.
